afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 082306
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
405 PM MST Tue Sep 8 2026

.UPDATE...
Updated Aviation

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Above normal temperatures will prevail through the rest of the 
work week resulting in widespread moderate Heat Risk and areas of 
major Heat Risk.

- Extreme Heat Warnings will be in effect for portions of the lower 
deserts through the end of the work week.

- Thunderstorm coverage is expected to increase during the latter 
half of the week across Eastern and Central Arizona, with slight 
chances becoming introduced for the South Central Arizona lower 
deserts by Thursday.

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Not much has changed in the current upper atmosphere conditions over 
the past 24 hours with the region remaining between a large 
troughing feature over much of Western CONUS, and an expansive 
ridging over the Southern Plains and Mississippi River Valley 
region. Mid to high level clouds continue to stream northeastwards 
through the late morning hours due to southwesterly flow aloft. 
However the flow will begin shifting out of the southeast as the 
subtropical high moves westwards towards the Four Corners region 
starting this afternoon. The subtropical high is expected to peak 
Wednesday, with H5 heights quickly building to 596-597 dam, near to 
at NAEFS climatological max for this time of year. This will help 
drive afternoon high temperatures across the lower deserts around 5F 
above normal for this time of year. Additionally, while 
southwesterly flow usually advects drier air into the region, 
Pacific tropical moisture was able to be pulled in keeping good 
moisture in the mid to upper atmosphere. This has lead to overnight 
cloud coverage hindering radiative cooling and PWATs have remained 
between 130-150% of normal, with morning dew points consistently 
reading in the mid 50s to low 60s. Due to these factors the 
overnight low temperatures are in the mid to upper 80s, or near 7F-
10F above normal, and providing very little relief in the heat 
throughout this week. Major HeatRisk has resulted across a large 
portion of the lower deserts and an Extreme Heat Warning is in 
effect for the Phoenix Metro, portions of South-Central and 
Southwest AZ including the Yuma area, and portions of Imperial 
County including the Imperial Valley. Extreme Heat Warnings expand 
slightly further north Wednesday along the Lower CO River Valley and 
surrounding communities. 

As mentioned earlier the subtropical high will begin shifting winds 
aloft out of the southeast starting today and will continue through 
the week, with daily gulf surges likely. A notable increase to 1000- 
700 mb mixing ratios will occur Wednesday night quickly increasing 
to 10-12 g/kg across SC AZ and even into the lower western deserts 
starting wednesday. Unfortunately, with the subtropical high 
expected to be directly over head, strong anticyclonic subsidence 
storms will struggle to develop in the low deserts, although not 
impossible. HREF models continue to show between a 30-50% chance of 
storms developing in southeastern AZ, and chances expand northwards 
into SC AZ, even into southern Pinal County by Late Wednesday, but 
with the ridge overhead it will remain conditional.  

&&

.LONG TERM /THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...    
Late this week is shaping up to be a more active period for monsoon 
thunderstorms across at least South-Central AZ. By Thursday, 
anticyclonic subsidence will begin to diminish as the subtropical 
high weakens overhead, and abundant low level moisture will remain 
in place through the rest of the week and linger into the weekend. 
Latest NBM guidance seems to favor Friday with the best chances for 
lower desert thunderstorms, which makes sense given the weaker 
subsidence aloft and plenty of moisture and instability to support 
numerous thunderstorms over the high terrain by the afternoon, 
sending outflows into the lower deserts and triggering additional 
thunderstorms by the evening. GFS bufr soundings indicate a good 
balance between CAPE and DCAPE Thursday evening, with values between 
1000-1500 J/kg, which is typically a good indicator for severe 
weather potential over the Valley. However, CIN may be a bit 
stronger than preferred, and the development of thunderstorms that 
can utilize this environment will be entirely dependent on the 
presence and timing of a sufficient lifting mechanism (i.e., 
thunderstorm outflow boundary). This conditional threat continues 
Friday, but with perhaps lower DCAPE and shallower inverted-V 
soundings. Strong thunderstorm winds, dense blowing dust, locally 
heavy rainfall resulting in instances of flash flooding, and 
frequent lightning will all be on the table for thunderstorm hazards 
later this week.

The forecast for this weekend into early next week is much less 
certain, however, a few more details are coming into focus tonight 
compared to the guidance available in previous forecast updates. 
Ensembles are in better agreement that mean troughing will establish 
over the Northwest US, pushing the northern stream and likely a 
series of upper lows and their attendant jet streaks as far south as 
the Great Basin. WPC cluster analysis reveals discrepancies on how 
far south the mean troughing will establish and how strongly 
negative the midlevel height anomalies will become over the 
Northwest US. The current consensus is for flow aloft to shift south 
to southwesterly as a result, meaning the more typical monsoonal 
pattern which briefly sets up this week will be short-lived, 
becoming something more akin to a transition season setup. This does 
not, however, mean that thunderstorm chances leave the forecast. 
Drying will begin to occur from west to east, but low level moisture 
will not be scoured out from Southern AZ. Thunderstorms will likely 
continue to favor development over prominent terrain features, and 
lower desert storm chances will be dependent on outflows or a nearly 
uncapped environment. As for now, NBM/WPC PoPs have come in lower 
this weekend compared to Thu/Fri, and timing of the better chances 
seems a bit unrealistic, reflecting the high uncertainty and 
nebulous forcing mechanisms. Regardless, the main message for this 
weekend into early next week will be continued thunderstorm chances 
over at least South-Central AZ higher terrain areas, but likely a 
decrease in activity from Thu/Fri due to the pattern shift and until 
southeasterly flow returns. 

With the subtropical high diminished and then displaced by Northwest 
US troughing this weekend, temperatures will follow a downward 
trend, attaining near normal values likely by Saturday or Sunday, 
ending the extreme heat conditions.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 2305Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
No major weather issues will exist through Wednesday evening under 
occasional mid/high cigs and patchy virga. Confidence is excellent 
that wind behavior will be similar to the past 24 hours with 
predominant west winds prevailing much later into the overnight 
than is usual, then resuming a W/NW heading by early afternoon. 


Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
No major weather issues will exist through Wednesday evening under 
occasional mid/high cigs and patchy virga/SHRA. Confidence in wind 
trends is only moderate with a tendency for a NW direction to 
become more SE to SW through time. Extended periods of nearly calm 
conditions may be common during this transition. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Above normal temperatures will prevail through the end of the work 
week, then temperatures are likely to decrease closer to normal over 
the weekend. Afternoon minimum humidities will generally range 
between 18-30% areawide through much of the week following fair to 
good overnight recoveries between 35-70%. Fairly typical diurnal 
winds with occasional afternoon upslope breeziness can be expected 
through Thursday, followed by an increase in southerly to 
southwesterly winds Friday into this weekend. Rain and thunderstorm 
chances will remain low and mostly limited to the eastern Arizona 
high terrain through midweek before slight chances become introduced 
to the lower deserts of at least the eastern districts during the 
latter half of the week.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...Extreme Heat Warning until 8 PM MST Friday for AZZ532.

     Extreme Heat Warning until 8 PM MST Thursday for AZZ531-535>544-
     546-548>551-559.

     Extreme Heat Warning from 10 AM Wednesday to 8 PM MST Friday for 
     AZZ530-533.

CA...Extreme Heat Warning until 8 PM PDT Friday for CAZ562-566-567.

     Extreme Heat Warning from 10 AM Wednesday to 8 PM PDT Friday for 
     CAZ569-570.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Ryan
LONG TERM...Whittock 
AVIATION...Benedict 
FIRE WEATHER...Whittock
